title: Runtime Certification and Query Sequestration Rider (Draft)
summary: Draft contract rider to be appended to vendor agreements that operate inference runtimes. Defines certification cadence, minimum operational controls, evidence delivery, and a query sequestration protocol for high-risk requests or legal holds.
body:
Purpose:
This Rider supplements the primary agreement between Redwood Inference ("Company") and the Vendor ("Provider") that provides inference runtime services. It defines operational assurance obligations, evidence deliverables, and an emergency query sequestration mechanism to protect Customer data, maintain auditability, and enable timely forensic response.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to any Provider-managed inference runtime (hosted, dedicated, or private-managed) used to process Customer queries or artifacts for the Company.
- Covers runtime controls (key management, logging, KV/prefix cache handling), evidence delivery, test certifications, and sequestration operations triggered by security events, legal holds, or regulatory demands.

Key definitions (for Rider only):
- Runtime Certification: formal evidence package demonstrating Provider controls, configuration, and test results for a named runtime instance.
- Query Sequestration: the ability to isolate, hold, and extract a specific subset of inference requests and associated ephemeral state (KV cache, session state) in a tamper-evident container for preservation and forensics.
- Tamper-evident evidence: logs and artifacts hashed and signed or accompanied by cryptographic proofs allowing verification of integrity.

Certification and evidence cadence:
1) Initial certification: Provider shall deliver a Runtime Certification within 30 calendar days of first production traffic for a new runtime instance. The package must include: inventory of runtime components, kernel/quantization profile, batch configuration, KMS key IDs, and a signed baseline log excerpt.
2) Quarterly attestation: Provider shall deliver a written attestation every 90 days confirming runtime configuration has not materially changed and that control checks passed (see control checklist below). Attestation must be signed by an operator and a security representative.
3) Ad-hoc evidence: Upon Company request (see response timelines), Provider shall produce targeted evidence, including raw or redacted logs, trace identifiers, and cache snapshots relevant to specific queries within the retention window.

Minimum operational controls (baseline):
- Identity & Access: Principle of least privilege for runtime operators; role-based access controls documented and periodically reviewed. Administrative access to runtime control plane must be protected by multi-factor authentication and logged.
- Key Management: All cryptographic keys used for encryption of persisted query logs and any persisted model artifacts must be under a KMS. Provider must support Customer-managed encryption keys (bring-your-own-key) for Private and Dedicated deployments where contractually required.
- Logging & Tamper-evidence: Request/response metadata (not full PII by default) must be logged with cryptographic integrity checks (e.g., HMAC or signed hashes). Logs required for forensic reconstruction must be retained in an immutable store for at least the configured retention window (see Data Retention below).
- Ephemeral Cache Controls: Runtime KV/prefix caches must be configurable to enforce TTLs. The default maximum retention for ephemeral KV cache must be no greater than 24 hours unless Customer explicitly configures otherwise and signs appropriate risk acceptance.
- Segregation: Customer request/response material must be logically separated in storage and access controls from derivative telemetry and model telemetry.

Query sequestration protocol (high-level):
When sequestration is invoked (see triggers), Provider will perform an ordered set of operations to isolate and preserve the requested query set and any associated ephemeral state:
1) Acknowledge: Provider will acknowledge receipt of an invocation within 4 business hours.
2) Snapshot: Provider will create a tamper-evident snapshot of the following (as applicable): request payloads, response outputs, KV/prefix cache segments associated with implicated sessions, routing metadata, and full host-level logs for the time window.
3) Isolation: The snapshot will be moved to a WORM (write-once-read-many) container or similarly immutable location with access strictly limited to forensic personnel agreed in writing by Company.
4) Delivery: Provider will deliver the snapshot (encrypted in transit) to Company or to a mutually-agreed third-party escrow within 72 hours of acknowledgment unless a legal constraint prevents transfer.
5) Access & Analysis: Company may request limited remote analysis by Provider under a pre-agreed playbook when transfer is not possible. Provider will provide a transparent query of the preserved artifacts and produce a forensic report within 10 business days, or sooner if the parties agree.

Sequestration triggers (non-exhaustive):
- Verified or suspected data exfiltration tied to inference traffic.
- Receipt of a legal hold or preservation notice from a Customer or regulator affecting specific queries or sessions.
- High-severity runtime compromise (e.g., kernel-level tampering, host compromise impacting KV cache integrity).
- Company security team reasonably suspects residual-PII exposure in runtime caches.

Response time commitments and SLAs for evidence requests:
- Acknowledgment: 4 business hours.
- Initial evidence packet (metadata + signed manifests): 72 hours.
- Full snapshot transfer (when permitted): 72 hours from acknowledgment.
- Forensic report: 10 business days from Company request (accelerated timelines to be used in incidents with active regulatory deadlines).

Audit rights and verification:
- Provider will allow Company or an independent auditor (NDA in place) to perform an annual on-site or remote control verification of the runtime, focusing on the controls enumerated in this Rider. The Provider is responsible for scheduling and delivering test evidence (e.g., reproduction of signed log chains, KMS key rotation proofs).
- For remote audits, Provider must provide API-based, read-only access to an evidence endpoint with credentialed access restricted to specific audit windows.

Data minimization and retention:
- Default policy: request/response payloads are not to be retained beyond the operating retention window unless specifically required for troubleshooting or sequestration.
- Retention windows: standard telemetry/metrics: 365 days; request metadata and signed manifests: 90 days; ephemeral KV cache snapshots: 24 hours unless tagged for sequestration.
- Redaction & minimization: Provider shall offer mechanisms to automatically redact or obfuscate PII fields prior to any long-term persistence, and document redaction rules applied.

Evidence integrity and chain-of-custody:
- All delivered evidence must include a signed manifest containing checksums (SHA-256 or stronger), timestamps, and the identity of the operator that performed the snapshot.
- Provider must maintain an auditable chain-of-custody log for evidence moves, including who accessed artifacts and when.

Escrow, hold, and termination mechanics:
- Escrow option: Provider must support delivery of evidence to an agreed escrow provider for long-term custody if Company requests.
- Hold: For legal holds initiated by Company, Provider shall suspend deletion of any implicated artifacts for the hold duration and provide confirmation to Company within 24 hours of hold initiation.
- Termination assistance: Upon contract termination, Provider shall provide an export of preserved artifacts (subject to any legal obligations) for a minimum transitional period of 30 days.

Limitations and exclusions:
- Provider is not required to copy or deliver third-party customer artifacts where doing so would breach third-party contracts or where transfer is prohibited by law.
- If Provider cannot comply with a sequestration transfer due to export controls, sanctions, or other legal prohibition, Provider will notify Company promptly and provide alternative measures (e.g., remote analysis).

Operational checklist (minimum items to verify during certification):
- KMS integration verified (keys used for persisted logs/model artifacts).
- KV cache TTLs configurable and enforced; default documented.
- Signed log chain configured and testable for a 7-day window.
- Administrative access audit and MFA verification.
- Immutable storage/WORM capability for evidence snapshots.
- Sequestration playbook tested in tabletop exercises within prior 12 months.

Evidence templates (deliverables):
- Signed manifest (SHA-256 entries), operator signature, timestamp.
- Metadata index: time window, runtime instance ID, host IDs, service versions.
- Forensic report template: summary, timeline, reconstructed query flow, artifacts preserved, recommendations.

Implementation timeline (provisional for new engagements):
- Negotiated as part of contract signature: 0–30 days for initial runtime onboarding and initial certification.
- Full playbook validation: within 60 days of production traffic.
- Quarterly attestations to begin after first certification cycle.

Billing and cost allocation for evidence operations:
- Routine attestations and quarterly certifications to be provided at no additional charge.
- Large-scale evidence preservation and cross-border transfers that materially increase Provider operational costs may be charged on a time-and-materials basis; Provider must notify Company and obtain prior approval for incremental charges.

Acceptance and changes:
- Any changes to the Rider that materially alter Company rights with respect to evidence, sequestration, or auditability require mutual written consent.

Sign-off (placeholders):
- Company Representative: _____________________ Date: __________
- Provider Representative: _____________________ Date: __________

Notes & open questions (to be resolved during negotiation):
- Default KV cache TTL: company to propose 24 hours as standard; provider to indicate exceptions.
- Cross-border transfer constraints and escrow options: specify allowed jurisdictions for escrow.
- Escalation path/SLR for accelerated forensic timelines during regulatory investigations.

Quick checklist for Legal/Procurement reviewers:
- Ensure definition of "sequestration" maps to technical snapshot set.
- Confirm retention windows align with Company policy and regulator expectations.
- Insert export-control carveouts if Provider hosts in restricted jurisdictions.
- Verify escrow provider options and encryption key hand-off process.

End of Rider (draft).
